The structure of Cu₂HgSe₄ crystallizes in the hexagonal space group P6₃/mmc (No. 194), with a unit cell containing 14 atoms—Cu₄Hg₂Se₈—distributed over three independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Cu centers coordinated by four Se neighbors, Hg centers by five Se neighbors, and each Se center by six neighbors (one Cu, two Hg, three Se). The neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 14 sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing contacts include corner- and edge-sharing between Cu and Se polyhedra, and corner, edge, and face sharing among Se-centered polyhedra.
